## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Mahākappinattheragāthā* (Thag 10.3) consists of the verses attributed to the elder Mahākappina within the *Theragāthā* collection of the Pali Canon [SuttaCentral]. The text has been translated into multiple modern languages, including an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato among nine translations in eight languages recorded on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].

Verses from the text share extensive textual parallels with the Dharmapada and Udānavarga traditions. Curated passage-level parallels identified by SuttaCentral include the fifteenth chapter (*Smṛtivarga* / "Reflection") of the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* (UV 15; UVS 15), the Tibetan *Udānavarga* (Uv Kg 15), and Chinese translations in the Taishō Tripiṭaka (T 210.6, T 212.16, and T 213.15) [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral also notes resembling verses in the Pali Dhammapada (Dhp 172, 173), the Gāndhārī Dharmapada (G-Dhp 97–134), the Patna Dharmapada, the *Aṅgulimāla Sutta* (MN 86), the *Aṅgulimālattheragāthā* (Thag 16.8), and related sections of Chinese and Sanskrit Udānavargas (UV 16; T 210.10; T 212.17; T 213.16) [SuttaCentral]. In automated text-reuse analyses, DharmaNexus identifies 11 matching segments between the verses (§0.4–10.5) and the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (Dutiyo bhāgo), as well as cross-language alignments with the Sanskrit Patna Dharmapada and the *Dhāraṇīsaṃgraha* [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
